elements.element: Preferred: renewal by mutual written agreement OR automatic 12-month renewal term
elements.evidence: "Each Order Form renews for twelve months"

elements.element: Preferred: Customer may opt out of automatic renewal on 30 days' notice
elements.evidence: "unless either Party gives thirty days' advance written notice before the end of the then-current term"

elements.element: Preferred: Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal
elements.evidence: No reminder obligation appears in 8.2 or 8.3; 8.3 only requires "at least ninety days' written notice of an increase"

elements.element: Preferred: price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%
elements.evidence: "only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index ... and three percent"
"Each Order Form renews for twelve months"

elements.element: Fallback: non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days
elements.evidence: "gives thirty days' advance written notice before the end of the then-current term" (30 ≤ 60)
"the lesser of the increase in the ... Consumer Price Index ... and three percent"

reasons: The locked target was preferred, but the preferred bargain also requires a Vendor reminder 60 days before each renewal; no such reminder mechanic exists anywhere in 8.2–8.3, so the preferred level is incomplete.

All fallback elements are satisfied on their material terms: automatic renewal, a 30-day (≤60) non-renewal notice window, and a CPI/3% uplift cap that is comfortably ≤5%. The clause therefore sits at or above the fallback and is acceptable.

The deterministic check reporting "number not found by the official literal pattern" appears to be a pattern artefact: the window is spelled out as "thirty days'" rather than numerically, and read literally it is 30 days.

The single replace operation changed only the notice period and added the anchor "before the end of the then-current term"; nothing else was touched, and the 12-month term, CPI/3% cap, 90-day increase notice and prepaid-period carve-out remain effective. Minimality and preservation of intent are satisfied.
Remaining gap (missing 60-day Vendor reminder) is a minor sub-element short of preferred wording and should be noted in the rationale rather than redlined further.
